LINE: Line. Feature or boundary line depicted on aeronautical charts; also used in SIGMET to describe a line of weather phenomena.
LM: Locator, middle. NDB (non-directional beacon) serving as the middle locator in an ILS instrument approach, typically co-located with or near the middle marker.
LMT: Local mean time. Mean solar time based on the local meridian, used in aviation for timekeeping and flight planning references.
LO: Locator, outer. NDB (non-directional beacon) serving as the outer locator in an ILS instrument approach, typically co-located with or near the outer marker.
LOC: Localizer. The lateral guidance component of an ILS (Instrument Landing System) providing azimuth guidance to the runway centerline.
LOSS: Airspeed or headwind loss. Abrupt reduction in airspeed or headwind component, typically encountered in wind shear or turbulence conditions.
LRG: Long range. Classification of aircraft or equipment capable of operating over extended distances without refueling.
LTA: Lower control area. Designated airspace below the upper control area boundary where air traffic control services are provided.
LTD: Limited. Qualifier indicating restrictions or constraints on equipment, operations, or airspace availability.
LTP: Landing threshold point. The point on the runway centerline at the beginning of the designated landing surface for an approach procedure.
LVE: Leave or leaving. Used in NOTAM and flight movement messages to indicate departure or exit from a location, airspace, or condition.
LVL: Level. Flight level or altitude reference used in air traffic control communications and flight plans.
LVP: Low visibility procedures. Aerodrome operating procedures designed to maintain safe operations when visibility is below standard minima, typically for Category II/III approaches.
LYR: Layer or layered. Description of cloud layers, atmospheric strata, or stacked airspace structure in meteorological and NOTAM reports.
MAA: Maximum authorized altitude. The highest altitude at which an aircraft may operate within a specific airspace or on a specific route segment.
MAG: Magnetic. Reference to magnetic north or magnetic direction, used in navigation headings, runways, and instrument procedures.
MAHF: Missed approach holding fix. The designated fix where an aircraft holds after executing a missed approach procedure, typically specified on instrument approach charts.
MAINT: Maintenance. Scheduled or unscheduled work on aircraft, ground equipment, or facilities to ensure continued airworthiness and operational readiness.
MAP: Aeronautical maps and charts. Published cartographic products depicting terrain, airspace, navigation aids, and instrument procedures used for flight planning and navigation.
MAPT: Missed approach point. The specified point in an instrument approach procedure at which the missed approach must be initiated if the required visual reference is not established.
MAR: At sea. Indication that a location, operation, or phenomenon is situated over maritime waters rather than land.
MATF: Missed approach turning fix. A designated fix in a missed approach procedure where the aircraft initiates a turn to proceed to the holding fix or alternate route.
MAX: Maximum. The highest permissible value of a parameter such as altitude, speed, weight, or temperature in operational limits.
MAY: May. The fifth month of the year, used in date notation in NOTAM and aviation documentation.
MBST: Microburst. An intense, localized downdraft of air that spreads radially upon reaching the surface, producing severe wind shear hazardous to aircraft during takeoff and landing.
MCA: Minimum crossing altitude. The lowest altitude at which an aircraft must cross a navigation fix or intersection when proceeding on an airway or route.
MCTR: Military control zone. Controlled airspace established around military aerodromes to protect military flight operations, equivalent to a control zone but under military ATC jurisdiction.
MCW: Modulated continuous wave. A continuous wave radio signal modulated with an audio frequency, used for station identification and Morse code transmission.
MDA: Minimum descent altitude. The lowest altitude, expressed in feet MSL, to which descent is authorized on a non-precision approach without visual reference to the runway.
MDH: Minimum descent height. The lowest height above the runway threshold elevation to which descent is authorized on a non-precision approach without visual reference.
MEA: Minimum en-route altitude. The lowest altitude between fixes on an airway or route that ensures adequate navigation signal reception, obstacle clearance, and communications coverage.
MEDEVAC: Medical evacuation flight. A flight dedicated to transporting injured or ill persons requiring urgent medical care, typically granted priority handling by ATC.
MET: Meteorological or meteorology. Pertaining to weather and atmospheric conditions; used in aviation for reports, forecasts, and operational planning.
MHA: Minimum holding altitude. The lowest altitude at which an aircraft may hold at a specific holding fix, ensuring obstacle clearance and airspace protection.
MHZ: Megahertz. Unit of frequency equal to one million hertz, used to express radio and navigation aid frequencies in aviation communications.
MIFG: Shallow fog. Fog layer less than approximately 2 meters deep that does not significantly restrict horizontal visibility at eye level, coded in METAR as MIFG.
MIL: Military. Pertaining to armed forces operations, aircraft, airfields, or airspace designated for defense purposes.
MIN: Minute. Unit of time equal to 60 seconds, used in aviation for flight times, fuel calculations, and operational timelines.
MKR: Marker radio beacon. A 75 MHz radio transmitter that radiates a vertical fan-shaped pattern to provide position fixes along an ILS approach path.
MLS: Microwave landing system. A precision approach guidance system operating in the microwave frequency band, providing azimuth, elevation, and distance information for aircraft landings.
MM: Middle marker. A 75 MHz marker beacon located approximately 0.5 to 0.8 nautical miles from the runway threshold on an ILS approach, indicating the point to begin the final descent.
MNM: Minimum. The lowest permissible value of a parameter such as altitude, visibility, or weather conditions required for a specific operation.
MNTN: Maintain. ATC instruction to keep a specified altitude, heading, speed, or configuration until further advised.
MOA: Military operating area. Designated airspace established for military training activities such as air combat maneuvers, weapons testing, or low-altitude operations.
MON: Above mountains. Indication that a location, phenomenon, or operation is situated over or in relation to mountainous terrain.
MOV: Move or moving or movement. Describes the translation of an aircraft, weather system, or airspace feature from one location to another.
MPS: Metres per second. SI unit of speed used in aviation meteorology to report wind speed, particularly in international METAR/TAF reports.
MRA: Minimum reception altitude. The lowest altitude at which an aircraft can reliably receive navigation signals from a specific aid while on a given route segment.
MRG: Medium range. Classification of aircraft or equipment with operational range capabilities between short and long range, typically suitable for regional operations.
MRP: ATS/MET reporting point. A designated geographic point, defined by latitude/longitude or navigation aid, at which aircraft are required to report position and meteorological conditions.
